ai.summary: The `version` string in `npm-app/release-legacy/package.json` was updated from `0.0.2-legacy.0` to `0.0.3-legacy.0`, reflecting routine release increment semantics for the legacy distribution channel. This bump carries forward recent repo URL, banner, and strict semver regex changes already landed in this release.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `npm-app/release-legacy/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `0.0.2-legacy.0` to `0.0.3-legacy.0` in the `codebuff` package manifest.

eli5.text: This release sharpens up how Freebuff builds and checks new versions, making the behind-the-scenes publishing process stricter and more reliable. The release tool now only accepts properly formatted version tags, which cuts down on mistakes during publishing. It also adds a secure debug session to the build process so developers can quickly investigate any issues that pop up while putting together the command-line tool. On the user side, the legacy command-line installer now greets you with a clear message telling you how to upgrade to the latest interface. If you are still on the old interface, you will be guided to install the new one. Overall, upgrading keeps you on the right path to the current tool and makes future updates smoother and less error prone.

ai.title: CLI build script defines NEXTPUBLIC flags
ai.summary: Added manual definition of NEXT_PUBLIC_* environment flags in cli/scripts/build-binary.ts. Ensures build-time constants like APP_URL and STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY are explicitly set with fallback defaults. Scope limited to CLI binary build process. Includes hardcoded fallbacks for production URLs and keys.

eli5.text: When the app builds you a tool that runs on your computer, it now bakes in the correct website addresses and payment keys it needs to talk to, so you don't have to supply them yourself. If a key is missing, safe defaults are used instead, and the tool no longer picks those settings up dynamically while it's running. This only affects the downloadable version of the app you install locally; if you use the web version in a browser, nothing changes for you. It's live today as part of the latest build.

ai.title: Remove CI debug shells and dynamic NEXTPUBLIC env collection in CLI
ai.summary: Removed hardcoded NEXT_PUBLIC_* environment variables in cli/scripts/build-binary.ts in favor of dynamic collection from process.env. Deleted four mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3 debug shell steps from .github/workflows/cli-release-build.yml. This prevents hardcoded fallbacks and removes SSH access in CI.

eli5.text: When the company releases updates to its command-line tool, it used to leave temporary remote terminals open during the build process; those have now been removed, so automated systems can no longer start debug sessions if something goes wrong during building. At the same time, instead of hardcoding specific configuration addresses into the tool, the build now collects them dynamically from whatever environment variables are present, preventing stale fallback addresses from being baked in if settings change.

ai.title: Fix compareVersions regex guard in release index
ai.summary: Inverted regex check in `compareVersions` within `npm-app/release/index.js`. Previously, valid numeric versions triggered an early `-1` return, causing incorrect sorting. Now only non-numeric versions return `-1`, allowing proper comparison of valid semver strings. Scope limited to release tooling logic.

eli5.text: When the release tool lines up version numbers to decide which one is newest, it was wrongly treating valid numbers like a broken entry and pushing them aside, which scrambled the order. The tool now only sets a valid version aside when the entry really isn't a number, so normal version numbers stay in the right spot and sort correctly. This only affects the internal release tooling that publishes packages, and it's already live.

eli5.text: This release sharpens the behind-the-scenes systems that power Freebuff, making upgrades smoother and the product more reliable for daily use. The release process now only accepts clean, properly formatted version numbers, so builds and updates install without confusion or errors. A new diagnostic tool was added to the build pipeline so developers can quickly investigate any problems that arise during releases. Users running the older legacy interface will see a clear prompt guiding them to upgrade to the latest version. Environment settings that control how the app connects to services are now pulled in automatically, which removes the need for hardcoded backup values and keeps configurations consistent. Finally, a small sorting fix ensures version numbers are compared correctly, preventing the wrong update from being offered to users.

ai.title: Add GPT-5 support to base2 agent orchestration
ai.summary: Introduced `isGpt5` flag in `createBase2` to switch model to `openai/gpt-5` and adjust spawnable agents. Added new `best-of-n-orchestrator-gpt-5` agent definition handling GPT-5 specific orchestration logic. Updated prompts and tool availability in `base2.ts` and `best-of-n-implementor.ts` to conditionally exclude `file-researcher` and `<think>` tags for GPT-5.

eli5.text: The assistant system can now choose to use a newer AI model called GPT-5 when working on coding tasks. This change is specifically enabled for internal agents that handle planning and writing code, and it is live today for those internal workflows. If you were looking at how the system picks which AI model to use, you'd see GPT-5 as an option and notice that the assistant now skips certain steps and tools it doesn't need when using this new model.

ai.title: Log NEXTPUBLIC env vars and drop underscore markdown markers
ai.summary: CLI startup logs sorted NEXT_PUBLIC_* environment variables to console. Markdown renderer fallback parser now ignores `_` and `__` emphasis markers, processing only `*` and `**`. Scope: `cli/src/chat.tsx`, `cli/src/utils/markdown-renderer.tsx`. Underscore-prefixed text previously parsed as emphasis now renders as literal.

eli5.text: When you start the program, it now prints certain settings (any starting with NEXT_PUBLIC_) that help figure out how it should behave, so you can see what special rules are active during that run. At the same time, bold or italic text written with underscores (like _this_ or __this__) will now appear exactly as typed instead of being reformatted, while text using asterisks (like *this* or **this**) still works for bold and italic.

ai.title: Add 10s timeout to codesearch to prevent hangs
ai.summary: Code search now enforces a 10-second timeout, killing the `rg` process with `SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL` if exceeded. This prevents indefinite hangs from overly broad patterns or complex searches. Implemented in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` and `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts`, returning a truncated output with an error message on timeout.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to search through a project's code, that search now stops on its own after 10 seconds instead of potentially running forever. If a search takes too long, you'll see an error message explaining what happened and suggesting the search was too broad, rather than watching a spinner indefinitely. This affects anyone using the search feature in the assistant.

The update applies to the core tool parameters, agent types, and initial agent templates.

eli5.text: The built-in help text for the code search tool no longer tells you to use a flag called --no-ignore that doesn't actually work anymore. If you use the search tool and open its list of optional flags to read what they do, you will no longer see the example telling you to type --no-ignore to look through files that your project deliberately hides; that flag is gone, so you cannot search those hidden files this way and the docs now correctly don't mention it. This only affects people typing optional search commands by hand in the tool's flags box; normal searching behaves the same.

ai.title: code-search switches to ripgrep JSON streaming with early stop
ai.summary: codeSearch tool replaces stdout line parsing with ripgrep --json streaming. Root cause: regex-based filename/line extraction failed on paths containing colons, hyphens, or non-UTF8 bytes, and patterns starting with `-` were misparsed as flags. Scope: sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts, sdk/src/__tests__/code-search.test.ts. Detail: adds `--no-config` to ignore user `.ripgreprc`, uses `--` to terminate flags, and kills the child process early when `maxResults` or `maxOutputStringLength` is hit, returning a `[Global limit of N results reached.]` suffix instead of buffering full stdout.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search through code, it now looks through your files in a more reliable way that doesn't break on file names containing colons, hyphens, or unusual characters. Instead of stopping mid-search when it finds enough results, it can now cut off early, so you get your answer faster without waiting for a full scan. This works today when you use code search in the SDK, and you'd notice it handles tricky file names and search patterns it used to skip or misread.

ai.summary: Spawner prompts for best-of-n-orchestrator.ts and best-of-n-orchestrator-gpt-5.ts now state 'Has no input prompt! It reads the context from the message history.' This clarifies that these agents derive context from history rather than accepting a direct user prompt. Internal agent definition change in .agents/base2/best-of-n/.

eli5.text: The orchestrator assistants that coordinate multiple implementation agents now have a clearer instruction in their setup: instead of expecting a direct prompt from you, they're told to pull context from the prior message history. Nothing about how they work changed, just the text describing what they do, making it explicit that you don't need to give them a fresh prompt; they already know what to work on from the conversation so far.

ai.title: Include meta-analysis in buffbench nightly email
ai.summary: Nightly buffbench evaluation emails now append a Meta-Analysis section containing overall comparison, per-agent insights, and key findings. `run-buffbench.ts` passes `metaAnalysis` in results, and `main-nightly.ts` destructures it to format the email body. Scope limited to `evals/buffbench` internal tooling.

eli5.text: The nightly email that the team gets each morning with buffbench test results now includes a new section at the end called a Meta-Analysis. It still shows the same per-agent numbers as before, but adds a quick overall summary, some notes about how each assistant performed, and the main takeaways from the run. This only affects the internal nightly email sent to the team (currently going to team@codebuff.com), and you’d see the new summary block after the usual results table if you opened the email. The change was made today in the internal tooling that builds and sends that email.

ai.title: Add taskcompleted tool for explicit agent turn termination
ai.summary: New `task_completed` tool added to agent runtime, requiring explicit invocation to end turns when enabled in agent templates. Logic in `run-agent-step.ts` enforces this constraint, falling back to `end_turn` or implicit completion only if the tool is absent from the template. Covers core constants, CLI/Web renderers, and type definitions across `common` and `packages/agent-runtime`. Includes updated `write_todos` guidance to prevent premature status marking.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes its work in a session, it now must explicitly signal that it is done using a new 'task completed' action instead of just stopping on its own. The developer notes that this action should be used when the request is fully fulfilled, when you need to ask the user a clarifying question, or when you are stuck. If you configure an assistant to have this action, it cannot end its turn any other way; only older assistants that lack the action will fall back to the previous behavior of ending turns implicitly or with an end-turn command. You would notice the difference as a new final step that requires a deliberate choice before a session closes.

ai.title: Add taskcompleted tool to base2-gpt-5 agent
ai.summary: Added `task_completed` tool to `base2-gpt-5` agent configuration in `.agents/base2/base2.ts`. Replaces previous instruction requiring tool calls in every response with explicit completion signal. Scope limited to `base2` agent definition for GPT-5 models.

eli5.text: When the GPT-5 version of the assistant finishes a task, it now has a dedicated 'done' signal it can send to clearly tell the system the job is complete, instead of relying on a general instruction to stop making tool calls. This only affects the GPT-5 variant of the base2 agent.

ai.summary: The base2 agent configuration in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` now sets `reasoningModel: { effort: 'high' }` when `isGpt5` is true. This ensures the GPT-5 orchestrator runs with maximum reasoning capability for complex coding tasks. Scope limited to the internal base agent definition; no CLI or Web UI changes.

eli5.text: When the internal orchestrator runs on the newest model, it can now spend more effort thinking through complex coding tasks. If you are an internal developer using the base2 agent with the new model, you will notice the assistant takes more time to reason before making changes on tricky problems. This is in place as of 2025-11-01 and only affects the internal base agent configuration, so your regular commands and interfaces remain the same.
